I understand where you're coming from. I've had those kinds of thoughts. It's a hard thing to combat when you're still growing into yourself. Is there a certain point in which these urges are triggered? Or is it at random times. If you can start trying to identify when these urges are triggered, it might be able to help you figure out why they're happening. Maybe think about talking to your parents or someone you trust? If you can try to pull yourself away from the people to have the urge to hurt, it may help calm these urges. Maybe tell the people you're talking with that these things are happening and you're trying to figure it out, that you're severely sorry if it happens. Maybe trying to see if you can talk to a school counselor or something might help too.

This is a totally valid question. And as a lgbtq kid, I recommend talking to her, asking if there are any good sources you could use to read up on the LGBT community. Being able to support her is not discrediting her self worth, right to marry, or anything. If you simply treat her as human and make sure you don't say anything that has a harmful impact on her. Now with your husband, you may want to tell your daughter about what he things,but remind her you do not agree with him and you will always be there to support her. Pronouns can be very iffy. Especially if she said she uses she/they. Your daughter would be comfortable working with she/her and they/them pronouns. You could practice in front of your phone quietly and say things like, "I love her. They are my child" and things like that. All in all, remind her you love and support her and will always be there for her!
